summary: dosfstools 4.2 mkfs.fat ported as MKFSFAT.BIN: pristine vendored (sha256 verified vs L4 pin), 4 transcribed sources + headers + first-party blkdev/termios glue in src/user/mkfs/, one tight Makefile block, ARM binary builds clean (148,024 B), cstyle clean (transcribeds excluded like sed), user build intact, host-functional proof fully green (ftruncate-only -C via strace, BPB/FATs/root at FAT12/FAT16 incl. acceptance 128 MiB, -C EEXIST, mtools mdir+mcopy round-trip byte-exact). In-OS smoke attempted and partially successful: MKFSFAT.BIN boots and runs, '-C' creates PROBE.IMG at the exact requested size with a fully-allocated FAT chain, but the content writes do not persist into the file's clusters (deterministic: zeros on raw disk after graceful QMP quit, and kernel 'cat' reads them back blank) — a kernel write-path gap for ftruncate-extended FAT16 files that wave 3 / the kernel lane must resolve before S3; the kernel's own ftruncate unit test only covers write->shrink->extend-readback, not extend-then-write. Also flags: mkfs.fat BLOCKS are 1024-byte units (acceptance DISK_BLOCKS for the frozen 128 MiB OUT.IMG is 131072, not the L4 sketch comment's 512-byte math).

bin.install_note: 8.3 name MKFSFAT.BIN matches the acceptance '/TOOLS/MKFSFAT.BIN' reference (L4 sketch + acceptance S3); staged on the boot disk at ::/MKFSFAT.BIN by the disk recipe

ftruncate_path.notes: Upstream 4.2's -C already is open(O_EXCL|O_RDWR|O_CREAT,0666) then ftruncate(dev, part_sector*sector_size + blocks*BLOCK_SIZE) (mkfs.fat.c main(), lines ~1869-1881); no dd and no SEEK_HOLE anywhere in 4.2. Port changes nothing there. Host strace of the ported binary proves: open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL) + ftruncate, zero fallocate/truncate/dd writes. In-OS (desktop console): -C created PROBE.IMG at exactly 1,048,576 B with a fully-allocated FAT chain (clusters 108..171, verified on raw disk), dir entry + size persisted; the metadata content writes (boot sector/FATs/root) did NOT persist into the chain's clusters (all-zero on raw disk after graceful QMP quit and in the kernel's own read-back) -- see in_os_smoke.

in_os_smoke.method: Minimal ARM boot disk assembled in-lane (mkfsfat_host -F 16 -C 1G + mtools + bootloader/BOOTAA64.EFI + kernel hobbyos.elf + desktop/console/sh/mkfsfat bins, uppercase 8.3 names); booted qemu-system-aarch64 (acceptance-section-5.1 line, own PID, no pkill; serial to file + QMP); drove via QMP input-send-event (run_console_test.py pattern): Apps menu -> CONSOLE.BIN -> typed 'mkfsfat -F 16 -C PROBE.IMG 1024'. Serial + framebuffer (ppm2png) + raw-disk extraction evidence. Shutdown by graceful QMP quit to rule out teardown-writeback.
in_os_smoke.result: PARTIAL - MKFSFAT.BIN loads and runs in-OS (serial [LAUNCH] MKFSFAT.BIN 148024B; console rendered 'mkfs.fat 4.2 (2021-01-31)' + full geometry: 2048 sectors, media 0xf8, 2 16-bit FATs, 4 sectors/cluster, drive 0x80). '-C' created PROBE.IMG with the exact requested size (1,048,576 B) and a complete FAT chain. BUT the boot-sector/FAT/root content bytes do not persist into the file's clusters: raw disk reads back all zeros after a graceful QMP quit, and the kernel's own 'cat PROBE.IMG' renders blank. So file creation + ftruncate-as-size + chain allocation work in-OS; write-persistence of data into a freshly-f truncated file does not. The kernel's ftruncate unit test (fs_test.c:173-227) covers write->shrink->extend-readback(zero-fill) but never extend-then-write -- exactly mkfs.fat's -C access pattern.
in_os_smoke.deferred_reason: The S3-gating in-OS round trip (MKFSFAT -C OUT.IMG then boot it) cannot pass until the kernel writes into ftruncate-extended FAT16 files persist (kernel/wave-3 fix, single-writer); documented precisely in src/user/mkfs/README.md for wave 3: (1) mkfsfat -F 16 -C OUT.IMG 131072 -> exit 0, 128 MiB OUT.IMG; (2) -C on existing file refuses (rm -f first); (3) extract with fat16img.py get and mdir -i / boot via Limine; (4) -n label incl. CP850 + default NO NAME; (5) the write-persistence fix must land in the kernel FS layer first (extend-then-write on FAT16).

notes: mkfs.fat BLOCKS argument is 1024-byte units (BLOCK_SIZE 1024 in mkfs.fat.c), so the acceptance recipe must use DISK_BLOCKS=131072 for the frozen 128 MiB OUT.IMG (131072 KiB), NOT the L4 sketch comment's 524288-sectors-for-256MiB math (that would produce a 512 MiB image). Measured cluster arms: 64 MiB->spc4 (L5 table's spc2 row was illustrative), 128 MiB->spc4 (matches L5 freeze), 256 MiB->spc8 (matches L5; the audit section 5.3 '8 KiB clusters at 256 MiB' guess was wrong).

Makefile hobbyos.bin is only produced inside the disk recipe (objcopy, Makefile:1803); the standalone kernel target is hobbyos.elf (TARGET at :331). Recorded because an early gate run 'make hobbyos.bin' printed RC=2 'No rule to make target'; rerun as 'make hobbyos.elf' -> KERNEL_BUILD_RC=0 (evidence/w2-mkfs-kernel-build.log).
Host native build reuses the same config.h/sources; harmless macro-redefinition warnings from glibc's <endian.h> on the HOST build only (ARM sysroot has no endian.h, ARM build warning-free).

Unit-test coverage gap flagged for the kernel lane: fs_test.c test_fs_ftruncate extends then reads zero-fill but never writes into the extended region -- extend-then-write is precisely what the in-OS -C path (and the whole S3 disk assembly) needs.
